schedule: always-on daemon (FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8775), a monitor-area resident: maintenance 03:30, fleet bring-up 07:00, nightly pipeline chain 16:00 on A-share trading days (all Asia/Shanghai; the 21:00 ZCode check verifies each pass)
notes: Server-cluster maintainer area (python -m server_cluster.maintainer; added 2026-11): the cluster's resident janitor + SCHEDULER. One scheduler thread, per-job fire groups: the shared maintenance pass (03:30 Asia/Shanghai, env MAINTAINER_FIRE_AT) — the log cleanup, the stats DB robocopy backup, the db_table_audit archive — the daily 07:00 fleet bring-up (env MAINTAINER_BRING_UP_AT) firing the monitor area's POST /residents/ensure-up with its monitor.service_audit row, and since the 2026-11 sh retirement the NIGHTLY PIPELINE CHAIN (env MAINTAINER_PIPELINE_AT, default 16:00, A-share trading days only — the whole pass skips on non-trading days): the monitoring → downloads → builds → analysis → strategy tiers (scripts/orchestration/*.json) driven serially through the monitor area's orchestration runner — an in-flight same-file run is adopted (waited out), a timed-out or lost tier aborts the chain, one monitor.service_audit row records every pass. RECOVERY SURFACE: an interrupted pass (maintainer restart) resumes from server_cluster/_state/nightly_pipeline.json; a pass with failures keeps its record as the worklist for GET /pipeline/last-pass (outcomes + remaining + running) and POST /pipeline/finish (finish remaining tiers); POST /jobs/nightly_pipeline/run with {tiers, force} reruns particular tiers. GET /health and /stats the standard liveness, GET /jobs the job catalogue with each job's last result. Also the cluster's ONE resident-process executor (restarts of every resident execute here). Serves its own lean app (no jobs surface, no residents), like the config area. One instance only — the registration guard auto-exits a second run.
